messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT AUTO-PAGE: GPU pool 'us-west-gpu-pool-2' saturation detected. autoscaler failing to provision new nodes (api errors). queue length spike > 12k requests. severity: P1. Paging: @elena_sre @devon_infra @alex_ng

alex_ng: seeing the same in dashboard — tail latency and 429s increasing. autoscaler put into backoff with repeated API 429s to cloud provider.

elena_sre: taking IC. quick checklist: 1) confirm customer impact 2) check autoscaler errors 3) check node driver/runtime health 4) mitigate by routing/fallbacks

devon_infra: autoscaler logs show: `PutInstanceGroupTargetSize failed: quotaExceeded` and also `RateLimitExceeded` from provider. maxNodes cap is currently 150 (org default). We're at 148. requests to add nodes hammered provider API -> transient rate limits.

sam_runtime: also noticing lots of driver OOMs and Xid errors on several nodes (NVIDIA 510.*). sample from node gpu-node-117 logs:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:07Z] driver: gpu0: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN (Xid 79)
[2026-03-15T09:12:08Z] oom_killer: task threadpool:1234 invoked oom-killer
[2026-03-15T09:12:09Z] nvml: device lost
```
Repeated across ~6 nodes. Kernel messages show cgroup mem high, processes pinned.

maria_pm: customers reporting increased errors in production -> top affected customers: beta-corp, chatly, docsummarize. can we estimate request loss or degradation window?

elena_sre: quick impact: 20-30% increased 429s for generation endpoints in us-west region over past 18m. some fallbacks to smaller models succeeded but many requests timed out. ops: please open SEV-Trend ticket and update status page.

ops-bot: Created ticket INF-2026-3071. Status page updated to "Degraded: Inference latency and errors in US-WEST".

devon_infra: mitigation options: A) increase org soft cap to 200 nodes (requires sales/infra approval, takes ~20-30m) B) route new traffic to other regions (us-east, eu-west) — but config changes to routing policy needed and may spike latency for sessions pinned to region C) attempt to respin affected nodes after draining nv driver, but autoscaler not adding replacements due to quota/rate-limit.

alex_ng: while we decide, can we enable emergency fallback policy that routes low-priority traffic to hosted model pool (cheaper but smaller)? that's quick config flip.

elena_sre: agree. sam, can runtime team gate requests to heavy models to reduce memory pressure? e.g. reject requests above 8k tokens chunk or cap concurrency per-request.

sam_runtime: yes we can enable a temporary throttle on max input length and per-connection concurrency. I'll push a runtime patch and feature flag now.

jc_eng: also seeing autoscaler repeated failures due to provider side rate-limits. we can introduce a small jitter + exponential retry to reduce hammering and request provisioning more slowly; but that's a medium-term fix. For now, I'll flip autoscaler to use warm standby nodes (if available) approach: mark some non-critical pools as spill targets and drain sessions there. requires feature flag flip.

elena_sre: plan of record (short): 1) enable runtime input/concurrency throttle (sam) 2) flip routing to allow low-priority spill to hosted pool (alex) 3) start node drain & respin for nodes with repeated Xid/oom (devon + sam) 4) request capacity bump from cloud (devon) 5) notify customers and continue telemetry

alex_ng: done — routing flag set to allow hosted spill for low-priority traffic. roll started at 09:20 UTC.

sam_runtime: pushed runtime throttle flag at 09:23 UTC: max_input_tokens=8192, per_connection_concurrency=2. seeing immediate drop in memory pressure on affected nodes.

devon_infra: draining gpu-node-115/117/119. kicking node reset job. sample command used:
```
# drain + cordon
kubectl cordon gpu-node-117
kubectl drain gpu-node-117 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# backend: restart driver daemonset on node
ssh node-117 'sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service'
```
Replacements pending but autoscaler still in backoff. opened provider support ticket to request immediate ramp.

oncall-bot: @elena_sre you have 30m remaining in rotation. Are you handing off later?

elena_sre: I'll stay until stabilization then hand to @jc_eng for next shift. jc, prep to pick up at 10:00 UTC.

maria_pm: customer comms: drafting message for beta-corp/chatly/docsummarize — will say degraded performance in us-west, we're mitigating and routing traffic. ETA: 1-2 hours depending on capacity ramp.

sam_runtime: after throttle, runtime logs show fewer OOMs. but we still see Xid 79 on one node intermittently. investigating kernel logs for memory leak in a specific model handler. attaching log snippet:
```
model-handler[pid=4521]: alloc failed for tensor (size=2.5GB)
[...]
```

jc_eng: I applied partial autoscaler retry tweak: increased backoff window and decreased provision batch size from 10 to 3. autoscaler accepted new policy at 09:36 UTC. provisioning requests now spaced out.

devon_infra: provider confirmed they removed rate-limit after support action. they granted ephemeral quota for +30 instances (proc ticket #CLD-8023). autoscaler made progress and added 12 nodes at 09:42 UTC.

elena_sre: putting incident into mitigation state. queue length plateaued and starting to fall. latency trending back down.

maria_pm: posting update to affected customers: "We've routed low-priority traffic to alternative pools and throttled large requests. New capacity is being provisioned; you may see reduced errors in the next ~20-30m."

alex_ng: monitoring — error rate back to ~3% above normal, dropping.

elena_sre: handoff notes for next oncall (jc_eng):
- cause: combination of provider rate-limits/quota + driver/runtime OOMs (Xid 79) reduced effective GPU capacity; autoscaler backoff amplified queue growth.
- mitigations applied: runtime throttle, routing spill, node drains + driver restarts, autoscaler backoff tuning, provider quota bump.
- follow-ups: 1) drive autoscaler rate-limit hardening (exponential jitter + smaller batches) 2) root-cause on model handler memory behavior -> reproduce locally 3) request permanent capacity increase or create warm standby pool 4) add a runbook step to automatically enable spill to hosted pool when queue > 5k for >10m

jc_eng: taking handoff at 10:00 UTC. will pick up the follow-ups and coordinate with runtime/infra.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: from elena_sre to jc_eng at 09:58 UTC.

maria_pm: postmortem ticket created INF-2026-3071-PM. I'll schedule postmortem meeting for tomorrow 1600 UTC.

elena_sre: closing thread here. thanks team :thumbsup:

jc_eng: noted, will follow-up on autoscaler tweaks and postmortem action items.
